L16: > Abstract:We introduce the concept of non-Archimedean metrics attached to a transcendental pseudoeffective cohomology class on a compact Kähler manifold. This is obtained via extending the Ross-Witt Nyström correspondence to the relative case, and we point out that our construction agrees with that of Boucksom-Jonsson when the class is induced by a pseudoeffective $\mathbb Q$-line bundle.
L17: > We introduce the notion of a flag configuration attached to a transcendental big class, recovering the notion of a test configuration in the ample case. We show that non-Archimedean finite energy metrics are approximable by flag configurations, and very general versions of the radial Ding energy are continuous, a novel result even in the ample case.
L18: As applications, we characterize the delta invariant as the Ding semistability threshold of flag configurations and filtrations and prove a YTD type existence theorem in terms of flag configurations.

L18@P0: 1. Introduction and results
L19@P0: In recent years, especially since the appearance of [4], the non-Archimedean approach
L20@P0: to K-stability has gained attention, as evidenced by recent works [10,13–15,17,34,47],
L21@P0: to name only a few papers in the fast expanding literature.
L22@P0: Studying K-stability for degenerate classes is a natural extension of the much studied ample case [4,18–21,30,60,61,70]. Recent works aim to understand existence of
L23@P0: canonical metrics in this context as well. Degenerate Kähler–Einstein metrics have
L24@P0: taken the forefront [29, 35, 48–50, 68], but one would think that the notion of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics also extends to big classes, as minimizers of the
L25@P0: K-energy functional. With the study still in its infancy [37,71], a better understanding
L26@P0: of K-stability of big classes is needed before substantial progress can be made. Our
L27@P0: work tries to fill some of this void.
L28@P0: Mathematics Subject Classification 2020: 32U15 (primary); 30G06, 32Q20 (secondary).
L29@P0-1: Keywords: non-Archimedean metrics, Kähler–Einstein metrics, test curves.T. Darvas, M. Xia, and K. Zhang 270
L30@P1: We propose a transcendental approach to non-Archimedean metrics, that allows
L31@P1: for their treatment even for a transcendental pseudoeffective class. Our analytic treatment has a number of advantages. The envelope conjecture of Boucksom–Jonsson
L32@P1: naturally holds in our context, immediately recovering the main result of [16], as a
L33@P1: particular case. We show that very general versions of the radial Ding energy are
L34@P1: continuous, and that finite energy non-Archimedean metrics can be approximated by
L35@P1: algebraic objects called flag configurations (that reduce to test configurations in the
L36@P1: ample case). The latter two properties allow to characterize the analytically defined
L37@P1: delta invariant using algebraic data, and provide a YTD type existence theorem for big
L38@P1: Kähler–Einstein (KE) metrics, without using the minimal model program, connecting
L39@P1: with recent work of the first and third authors [29].
L40@P1: Transcendental non-Archimedean metrics. To state our main results, we fix some
L41@P1: terminology. Let X be a connected compact Kähler manifold and  a smooth closed
L42@P1: real .1; 1/-form representing a pseudoeffective cohomology class ¹º. We denote by
